designs.title: No.
designs.why: Instant read from across the shop: a smug cat draped over a chunky 'NO' and pawing the ball that serves as the full stop. The joke is attitude, not a pun, so it sells to cat people of every age. The tabby-stripe fill in the letters ties type and cat together. Linework is confident and clean at full size, and it works in one ink on both white and black tees. Holding it back at $50: it prints small and high on the tee (a wide, short block that uses only the top half of the canvas), so it looks like a modest chest graphic rather than a statement piece. The very fine hatching in the tail and the ledge shadow is also likely to fill in or break up in screen print, especially white ink on black.
designs.fix: Scale the artwork up so it fills more of the print area (roughly 20-30% wider, sitting a little lower on the back), and coarsen the tail and ledge hatching to thicker, fewer lines so it holds up in one-ink screen print.
